items.actual_behavior: Linear selects the ordinary .weight path, whose get_tensor call reaches convert_dtype. That function rejects F8_E4M3 as an unknown dtype. The inspected FP8 headers also contain projection weight_scale_inv tensors that this loading path never reads. This is an existing format limitation exposed by the newly recognized architecture, not evidence that the commit promised FP8 support.
items.affected_limits: Qwen3 dispatch at110 and six inspected FP8 variants only; no continuous range asserted.

items.description: Architecture registration does not provide a loader for the two published FP8 variants.
items.trigger: Load either reference -FP8 checkpoint through the new model builder and ordinary SafetensorsCollection.
items.expected_behavior: A compatible loading path would decode FP8 weights using their scale tensors.
items.actual_behavior: Q's .weight passes name detection, but get_tensor calls convert_dtype, which raises ValueError('Unknown dtype F8_E4M3'). The .weight_scale_inv tensors are not requested.
items.affected_limits: Two inspected published variants; sampled layer 0 projections and head, not every shard. No continuous affected range asserted.

items.description: The two published GPTQ variants store names that Linear.load does not consume.
items.trigger: Load either reference -GPTQ-Int4 checkpoint through Qwen3MoeModel.
items.expected_behavior: A compatible loader would recognize and decode GPTQ's qweight, qzeros, scales and g_idx.
items.actual_behavior: Neither the EXL3 group nor q_proj.weight matches; the first attention Linear raises 'No tensors found for model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj matching supported quantization format.' All sampled GPTQ projection auxiliaries remain unread, although their dtypes are recognized.
items.affected_limits: Two inspected published variants; sampled layer 0 projections and head, not every shard. No continuous affected range asserted.

items.description: The utility implicitly requires existing quantization_config metadata but does not validate that precondition before writing artifacts.
items.trigger: Invoke recompile on an otherwise supported input whose config.json lacks quantization_config and whose assembly reaches metadata writing.
items.expected_behavior: Reject unsupported input before writing, or supply complete metadata arguments.
items.actual_behavior: The utility supplies neither cal_rows nor cal_cols nor apply_out_scales. The compiler's fallback accesses cal_rows and raises KeyError after shard writing and auxiliary-file copying.
items.affected_limits: Source-supported conditional reach and scalar transcription only; no checkpoint recompilation or inference executed, no continuous affected range established.

items.description: A retained candidate can still allocate different K and V bitrates, contrary to the commit's stated goal.
items.trigger: Attention-only allocation with Q/K/V/O weight counts 256/128/128/256, target 3 and incoming surplus 640.
items.expected_behavior: K and V receive equal bitrates if the stated goal is universal.
items.actual_behavior: The patched allocator selects 3/4/5/4 and returns surplus 1.
items.affected_limits: Only the individually evidenced observations; no continuous descendant range asserted.

items.description: regularize requires a policy key that the existing quantization test does not supply.
items.trigger: test_quant_dequant reaches regularize with its unchanged K/seed-only quant_args dictionary.
items.expected_behavior: The repository caller supplies the new policy or omission defaults to automatic mode.
items.actual_behavior: quant_args['apply_out_scales'] raises KeyError. The test also already lacks devices, required later by the parent implementation; this is an additional incompatibility, not evidence that the test previously passed.
items.affected_limits: Only the individually evidenced observations; no continuous descendant range asserted.

items.description: Omitted resume arguments overwrite saved checkpoint interval, devices and ratios with parser defaults.
items.trigger: Resume without explicitly repeating stored non-default values.
items.expected_behavior: The guide says saved arguments are restored except selected overrides.
items.actual_behavior: Defaults 60, "0", "" replace stored values; devices warns, ratios does not.
items.affected_limits: Only individually evidenced observations; no continuous interval asserted.

items.description: Checkpoint-oriented block scales are not transposed alongside their weights.
items.trigger: An eagerly loaded checkpoint supplies a scale grid aligned with its original [out_features,in_features] weight rather than the internal transposed matrix.
items.expected_behavior: Preserve each weight block's associated scale through transposition.
items.actual_behavior: A rectangular grid can fail the shape assertion; a square asymmetric grid passes but assigns off-diagonal block scales to the wrong blocks.
items.affected_limits: Only the individually evidenced observations; no continuous descendant range asserted.

items.description: The new scoring loop does not preserve the native evaluator's tighter temporary lifetimes.
items.trigger: Score at least two rows successfully, so that an earlier row has left a `log_probs` tensor bound when the next forward starts.
items.expected_behavior: Release the completed row's log-probability reference before cache cleanup and the next forward, as `eval/ppl.py` does.
items.actual_behavior: The reference survives the cache-cleanup call and remains bound through the next forward until the next `log_softmax` result is assigned. Separately, `.float() + 1e-10` is an out-of-place addition rather than the parent's `+=`, so it can require another full scoring-sized tensor during the addition.
items.affected_limits: Source shows the reference lifetime. GPU allocation, peak memory, and out-of-memory behavior were not measured.

items.description: The output-padding branch prevents simultaneous input padding from copying into a correctly bounded destination.
items.trigger: Load an ordinary 130-by-130 weight with default pad_to=128.
items.expected_behavior: Copy into the leading 130-by-130 region of a zero-filled 256-by-256 matrix.
items.actual_behavior: The output-width condition selects padded[:130, :], a 130-by-256 destination, for the 130-by-130 source; the input-column branch is skipped.
items.affected_limits: Only the individually evidenced observations; no continuous descendant range asserted.

items.description: The advertised progress interfaces cover autosplit loading but silently omit explicit-device loading.
items.trigger: Call load(device=..., callback=...) or iterate load_gen(device=...).
items.expected_behavior: Receive callback or iterator progress for the selected loading mode.
items.actual_behavior: The device branch calls unchanged _load_single(progressbar, device), which neither invokes the callback nor yields progress. Iterating load_gen still performs loading but produces no progress tuples.
items.affected_limits: Only the individually evidenced observations; no continuous descendant range asserted.

items.description: Group detection does not compose the same disk-plus-memory availability offered by individual lookup.
items.trigger: A requested group is complete only across the union of tensor_file_map and new_tensors, for example disk trellis plus memory su and sv.
items.expected_behavior: If group detection is intended to reflect individual lookup availability, this group would be recognized.
items.actual_behavior: has_tensor_group returns false because neither source independently contains the complete group. Linear.load_exl3 consequently declines that storage layout.
items.affected_limits: Only the individually evidenced observations; no continuous descendant range asserted.

items.expected_behavior: The declaration should match the available definition.
items.actual_behavior: The declared five-argument overload has no matching definition in the inspected tree. Both discovered repository calls use the new definition locally, so this is not evidence of a current internal build failure.

items.expected_behavior: Return the ordinal list, as the parent implementation did.
items.actual_behavior: The function falls through and its cache stores None. self.id_to_ord is still populated. Whole-parent search found only the constructor call, which discards the return, so no inspected internal consumer fails on this change.

items.description: Root setup.py passes absolute extension source paths to setuptools; issue #2 reports its wheel build rejecting these paths.
items.trigger: Build a wheel using setuptools path validation, as reported in issue #2 with Python 3.12 and PyTorch 2.6.
items.expected_behavior: Extension source paths supplied through setup() are relative to the setup script directory.

items.description: The integer-call defect in Cache.detach_from_model's mismatched-layer assertion persists through commit 89f6401, which does not touch cache.py.
items.trigger: Call Cache.detach_from_model with assertions enabled and a model whose cache-layer count differs from the cache's count.
items.expected_behavior: Raise AssertionError that reports the incompatible cache-layer counts.
items.actual_behavior: The failure-message expression invokes integer model_num_layers and raises TypeError before the intended assertion diagnostic.

items.description: Commit 5498926 documents disk_lru_cache with module-relative storage, function-name identity and string-representable arguments, while the implementation uses the launcher directory, an explicit filename and JSON serialization.
items.trigger: A caller relies on the new docstring where launcher and module directories differ, the explicit cache filename differs from the function name, or an argument is printable but not JSON serializable.
items.expected_behavior: Documentation accurately identifies sys.argv[0]-relative storage, the explicit filename namespace and JSON-serializable arguments.
items.actual_behavior: The new docstrings describe different storage, naming and argument contracts from the unchanged implementation.

items.description: DeciLM initially passes query-head group size as the KV-head count; the fix derives KV heads as query heads divided by group size.
items.trigger: Active attention with positive evenly dividing group size, where group size differs from query-head count divided by group size.
items.expected_behavior: KV-head count represents the number of query-head groups.
items.actual_behavior: The original direct mapping changes K/V projection widths and reshape dimensions for noncoincident group sizes.

items.description: The root conversion code prefixes a relative work directory twice when saving converted module tensors, while compilation reads from the singly prefixed qtensors directory.
items.trigger: Conversion uses a relative work_dir and saves a converted module tensor through the root main/save_tensor call chain.
items.expected_behavior: Converted module tensors are written under work_dir/qtensors, the directory created by prepare_env and read by compile_model.
items.actual_behavior: main passes work_dir/qtensors/<key>.safetensors to save_tensor, which joins work_dir again and targets work_dir/work_dir/qtensors/<key>.safetensors. The inspected code does not create that doubled parent directory; the write outcome itself was not executed.

items.description: Commit c8b4bd5 changed Linear.quant_format_id from EXL3 to exl3 while the sidecar generator still compared against EXL3; commit 756ce86 restores agreement by changing the consumer comparison to exl3.
items.trigger: Generate quantization_config.json for a leaf Linear whose primary-key storage satisfies is_exl3_storage at the affected commit 19 tree.
items.expected_behavior: The sidecar records quant_format and bits_per_weight for the EXL3 Linear leaf while serializing the lowercase format value.
items.actual_behavior: At commit 19, Linear returns exl3 while the unchanged consumer tests for EXL3, skipping the guarded fields. Commit 20 changes the test to exl3.

items.description: The explicit package list still omits the generator filter subpackage that installed code imports eagerly.
items.trigger: Import `exllamav3` from an installation that follows the explicit package list and does not otherwise expose the filter source, for example when starting the chat example outside the checkout.
items.expected_behavior: The installed distribution provides `exllamav3.generator.filter` so that the generator and public filter exports can be imported.
items.actual_behavior: Through 326, setup.py omits exllamav3.generator.filter while the generator eagerly imports it. Issue #62 reports the resulting missing module in an installed package. At 327 the explicit package list includes the subpackage.
items.affected_limits: Introduction and 326 source checked. The affected released distribution and continuous range were not verified.

items.description: The root native binding translation unit includes quant/exl3_gemv.cuh, which is absent from the published source tree.
items.trigger: Compile bindings.cpp against the checked-in source and normal include paths, without supplying an external replacement header.
items.expected_behavior: Every unconditional project-local include required by the native translation unit resolves from the published build inputs.
items.actual_behavior: The compiler cannot resolve the missing quoted header; commit 6 removes that include.

items.description: Commit 4d82aab independently rounds each requested multi-GPU tile share to a multiple of 16 and assigns the discrepancy to the final share, which can make that share negative.
items.trigger: A multi-GPU quantization call with 32 tiles and device_ratios [3, 3, 3, 1].
items.expected_behavior: Every size passed to torch.split is a nonnegative integer and the sizes sum to the tile count.
items.actual_behavior: The arithmetic produces [16, 16, 16, -16] and passes it to torch.split before the later positive-share guard.

items.description: The human_time helper introduced at commit e0f26ed rounded minutes to the nearest hour and then subtracted that rounded hour count, producing negative displayed minutes for half of each hour-scale input cycle until commit 825408b changed both divisions to floor division.
items.trigger: At affected commit e0f26ed, conversion prints a remaining-time estimate whose rounded minute count modulo 60 is at least 30, beginning around 29 minutes 30 seconds.
items.expected_behavior: A nonnegative duration representation whose hour and minute components describe the positive estimate.
items.actual_behavior: At the introduction, the formatter emitted outputs such as '1 hour, -30 minute', '1 hour, -1 minute', and '2 hours, -30 minute'.

items.description: quantize_exl3 assigns proxy_err_2 but returns the unbound proxy_err name.
items.trigger: A quantize_exl3 invocation completes quantization, metric evaluation and tensor packing and reaches its return.
items.expected_behavior: Return quantized weight, computed proxy error and packed tensors.
items.actual_behavior: Return references proxy_err, which has no binding in the function or module; source indicates NameError.

items.description: Two sampler modules import override from the standard-library typing module even though typing.override was added only in Python 3.12, making the import chain incompatible with Python 3.11.
items.trigger: Run import exllamav3 on Python 3.11 at an affected tree and reach the generator sampler package imports.
items.expected_behavior: The package import resolves its declared typing_extensions dependency or otherwise declares an interpreter range that excludes Python 3.11.
items.actual_behavior: exllamav3 imports generator.sampler; its package imports sampler.py and custom.py, which import override from typing. Official Python 3.12 documentation identifies typing.override as newly added in 3.12, so that name is absent from typing on Python 3.11.

items.description: Commit 72e88ae makes quant_args["devices"] mandatory in the EXL3 quantization path while tests/test_quant_fn.py omits it; the incompatibility persists at commit 4d82aab, whose new device_ratios key uses .get and adds no second missing-key failure.
items.trigger: tests/test_quant_fn.py calls Linear.convert_exl3 with its two-key quant_args dictionary at either verified affected revision.
items.expected_behavior: Repository callers provide every required quantization argument or the implementation supplies a compatible default.
items.actual_behavior: The test caller reaches an unconditional quant_args["devices"] read and raises KeyError: 'devices' before quantization proceeds.

items.description: Commit 72e88ae computes golden-section progress with int(delta2 / delta1), causing every contraction update to report 100 while the search continues.
items.trigger: g_scale_gss performs any interval contraction with a visible ProgressBar.
items.expected_behavior: Intermediate contractions report progress below completion until the search terminates.
items.actual_behavior: Because the contracted-width ratio is between zero and one, int(delta2 / delta1) is zero and pb.update receives 100 on every iteration.

items.description: Commit ae9f910 documents --shard_size as a float and says zero disables sharding, while the preexisting parser requires an integer and the allocator treats zero as a zero-byte threshold that creates a new shard after each nonempty module group.
items.trigger: Follow the new guide by passing --shard_size 1.5, or pass zero while compiling multiple modules with positive tensor sizes.
items.expected_behavior: The documented fractional value is accepted, and zero produces an unsharded output.
items.actual_behavior: Argparse rejects fractional text. With zero, every positive module after a nonempty shard causes another shard because no disabling branch exists.

items.description: From the root revision, Tokenizer.decode_ removes EOS before testing for it and filters extended IDs outside the backend vocabulary before special rendering; both behaviors persist unchanged at commit 40fb78f.
items.trigger: Decode a sequence containing EOS followed by ordinary tokens, or request special rendering of a mapped extended ID at or above the backend vocabulary size.
items.expected_behavior: The explicit EOS truncation branch discards the suffix, and mapped extended tokens survive to special rendering.
items.actual_behavior: EOS is removed before the truncation test, so suffix tokens remain; the vocabulary-bound filter discards out-of-backend extended IDs before dictionary rendering.

items.description: From the root revision, Tokenizer.decode documents a string return for batch size one but returns a one-element list for every rank-two one-row tensor; the mismatch persists unchanged at commit 40fb78f.
items.trigger: Pass a rank-two tensor with one row to Tokenizer.decode.
items.expected_behavior: The documented contract returns a string when batch size is one.
items.actual_behavior: The rank-two branch always constructs and returns a list, including for one row.

items.description: Commit 89f6401 permits both transformer branches to be absent, but allocate_transformer divides by zero before its explicit empty-permutation assertion.
items.trigger: Call TransformerBlock.allocate_q or allocate_transformer with neither attention nor MLP projections.
items.expected_behavior: Return an empty strategy or explicitly reject an empty block before budget division.
items.actual_behavior: The projection list has zero elements, so budget / numel raises ZeroDivisionError before the later Logic error assertion.

items.description: Commit 89f6401 makes transformer branches optional but leaves each branch input y initialized only when its optional input norm exists.
items.trigger: Run a present attention branch without attn_norm, or a present MLP branch without mlp_norm.
items.expected_behavior: A branch without input normalization receives the current residual state x.
items.actual_behavior: Attention without its norm and MLP without its norm when attention is absent read unassigned y; an unnormalized MLP after attention reuses the attention output rather than the updated residual state.

items.description: Commit 11 removes tabulate from requirements.txt while two static imports remain and setup.py does not declare it; at commit 08cf8e9 the memory diagnostic import moves to function entry without adding a declaration.
items.trigger: Call list_gpu_tensors, or run science/qgemm_benchmark.py, in an environment without tabulate.
items.expected_behavior: Dependencies needed by these workflows are declared or their separate installation requirement is made explicit.
